name: Indapamide
mechanism: Acts on distal convoluted tubule causing natriuresis and vasodilation
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30), severe hepatic impairment, hypokalaemia, gout
interactions: NSAIDs (↓ effect), lithium (↑ toxicity), digoxin (hypokalaemia ↑ toxicity)
monitoring: U&Es, glucose, uric acid, blood pressure
pharmacokinetics: Well absorbed, hepatic metabolism, long half-life allowing once daily dosing
clinicalPearls: Preferred thiazide-like in UK for hypertension. Less metabolic disturbance than bendroflumethiazide
indication: Hypertension (first-line with ACEi/ARB or CCB), mild heart failure
